notes.text: A flaw was found in the `os.Root` functionality of Go on Unix systems. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass intended directory restrictions by crafting a path that ends with a symbolic link and a trailing slash. When a file is opened in `os.Root` with such a path, the symbolic link is improperly followed, potentially leading to access to locations outside of the defined root directory. This could result in information disclosure or unauthorized file system access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in Go's os.Root implementation. On Unix systems, `os.Root.Open()` improperly follows symlinks to locations outside the root directory when the path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., root.Open("symlink/")). This is because `openat()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` does not prevent symlink resolution when the path has a trailing /. An attacker able to create symlinks within an os.Root directory could use this to read or write files outside the intended root. The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected. This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

The following symbols are affected:
* `OpenInRoot`: Opens a file or directory within an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Create`: Creates a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Open`: Opens a path relative to an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenFile`: Opens a file with specified flags and permissions inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenRoot`: Opens a sub-root directory from an `os.Root`.
* `Root.ReadFile`: Reads a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.WriteFile`: Writes a file inside an `os.Root`.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.
notes.title: Statement

This could lead to excessive CPU consumption on the system processing the malformed header, impacting service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a software component used for parsing Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) in Node.js applications. This vulnerability arises from an issue in how fast-uri processes the scheme part of a URI, specifically when it contains special characters that are percent-encoded. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious URI, causing the parser to misinterpret the host, which can lead to serious security risks. These risks include unauthorized redirection to external websites, server-side request forgery (SSRF) where the application makes unintended requests to internal or external resources, and bypassing security policies.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: URI parsing flaw enables server-side request forgery and redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A host confusion vulnerability was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. The parser runs a legacy decoding pass over the scheme component and never re-escapes the result. As a consequence, an input whose scheme carries percent-encoded slashes parses as having no authority (undefined host), yet resolving or normalizing that same input emits a network-path reference with an attacker-chosen authority. Applications that normalize or resolve untrusted URLs before a redirect check, host allowlist, or outbound request decision can be steered to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF), open redirect, or address-policy bypass. Additionally, a normalized URI in a response header can carry injected carriage return line feed (CRLF) characters, enabling HTTP response splitting attacks such as cache poisoning or session hijacking. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici's BalancedPool component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate validation. The BalancedPool constructor incorrectly processes its options, silently discarding custom certificate validation functions. Consequently, a peer with an otherwise untrusted certificate may be accepted, potentially compromising the integrity of secure communication.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: TLS certificate validation bypass in BalancedPool via dropped connect options
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw only affects applications that construct an undici BalancedPool with a function-valued connect or tls option — for example, a custom checkServerIdentity callback or connector used for certificate pinning across multiple upstreams. Client, Pool, Agent, and RoundRobinPool destructure these options before the internal JSON-based clone and are not affected. An attacker able to present, on the network path, a TLS endpoint whose certificate the application's custom validator was written to reject — but which still satisfies Node.js's default hostname and chain checks — can have that certificate silently accepted when the connection goes through BalancedPool, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack against affected connections.
This affects undici versions from 7.24.1 up to 7.29.1 and from 8.0.0 up to 8.10.2.

This flaw is present in the undici HTTP client library used by Node.js. When an application composes undici's Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly onto a Client or Pool object (rather than onto an Agent), the library's internal cache and in-flight-request deduplication keys omit the destination origin. As a result, a cached or in-flight response captured for one upstream origin can be returned for a request intended for a different, trusted origin whenever the method, path, and relevant headers match. In the most severe demonstrated scenario, this allowed an attacker-controlled JWT to be accepted by the application as though it had been validated against a legitimate, trusted issuer, without that issuer ever being contacted — resulting in a full authentication bypass.
Exploitation requires that the affected application attach the Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly to a Client/Pool — the default Agent-based dispatch path is not affected, since Agent already carries the origin in its dispatch options — and that an attacker can influence or collide with the cache/deduplication key for at least one origin the application communicates with.).

A remote server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by initiating a Transport Layer Security (TLS) renegotiation and presenting a certificate with a mismatched hostname. Because the client application fails to properly handle the resulting verification error, an uncaught assertion is triggered, terminating the client process and disrupting active network requests.

notes.text: undici: undici: Denial of Service via TLS renegotiation with mismatched certificate
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as an Important severity flaw for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote server can terminate a client Node.js process, halting all concurrent tasks and in-flight operations. In typical Red Hat deployments, containerized microservices and administrative consoles rely on undici or runtime fetch APIs to communicate with external web endpoints. Exploitation requires the client application to establish an outbound TLS 1.2 connection to a malicious or compromised endpoint that initiates session renegotiation with a non-matching certificate. Workloads communicating strictly with trusted endpoints or utilizing TLS 1.3 connections are inherently protected, as TLS 1.3 does not permit server-driven renegotiation.

cwe.name: Origin Validation Error

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When an application configures redirect handling alongside a shared cache, responses received after cross-origin redirects are incorrectly stored under the initial request URL. A remote attacker who controls a redirect destination can exploit this vulnerability to poison the shared cache, serving malicious content to subsequent users requesting trusted URLs. Additionally, this behavior can result in information disclosure if private or user-specific responses are cached and delivered to unauthorized callers.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Cache poisoning and information disclosure via improper cross-origin redirect caching
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because successful exploitation enables remote attackers to achieve shared cache poisoning and unauthorized cross-user data exposure across network boundaries without requiring elevated privileges. Within Red Hat environments shipping Node.js runtimes and associated container services, undici is utilized as an HTTP client backend. However, exploitation requires a specific application architecture where an originless dispatcher chains redirect processing ahead of a shared cache store, rather than the default standalone client configurations. Deployments that do not implement shared caching across multi-origin redirect flows or that isolate cache storage per origin remain unaffected by this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. In typical Red Hat environments, many bundled container services connect exclusively to controlled internal infrastructure, substantially reducing the likelihood of encountering an adversarial endpoint.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When an application sends a request to a malicious remote server, the server can return a response with excessive content encodings and immediately close the connection. Because the underlying response stream is left unhandled, this abrupt closure triggers an unhandled error that causes the application process to crash. Consequently, an attacker operating a remote server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS), terminating the application even if standard error handling is implemented.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Denial of Service via unhandled stream error on excessive content encodings
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote server can trigger an unhandled runtime error that abruptly terminates the parent Node.js process, bypassing application-level catch blocks. In Red Hat products and containerized workloads running affected Node.js runtimes, the flaw impacts services executing outbound HTTP calls to untrusted or external third-party endpoints. Conversely, deployments where applications only interact with verified internal endpoints or do not fetch content from untrusted remote hosts are not exposed to this denial-of-service condition.

cwe.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent. The NewKeyring() function, which creates an in-memory keyring, failed to enforce the ConfirmBeforeUse constraint on keys. This allowed keys configured to require user confirmation before use to perform signing operations without any prompt or indication to the user. Consequently, an attacker could potentially bypass intended security controls, leading to unauthorized cryptographic signing actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent: Security bypass due to unenforced key confirmation

notes.text: Red Hat rates this issue as Moderate with RH CVSS 5.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N). A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent where the in-memory keyring returned by NewKeyring() silently accepted SSH agent keys with the ConfirmBeforeUse constraint but did not enforce interactive confirmation before signing. Exploitation requires local access and low privileges on a system where an affected application uses NewKeyring() with ConfirmBeforeUse. Most Red Hat products that bundle golang.org/x/crypto do not use the ssh/agent ConfirmBeforeUse feature in their supported execution paths. The upstream CISA CVSS 9.1 assumes a broader network attack context that does not reflect Red Hat product deployment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.

notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in the crypto/tls component. This vulnerability occurs during Transport Layer Security (TLS) session resumption when certificate authority (CA) settings are modified between the initial and resumed handshakes. An attacker could exploit this to bypass certificate validation, allowing a client or server to establish a connection that should have been rejected. This could lead to an authentication bypass under specific conditions.

notes.text: crypto/tls: crypto/tls: Incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is a moderate flaw because it only occurs under specific conditions, such as TLS session resumption with runtime changes to certificate authority settings. Exploitation is not straightforward and requires a controlled setup. The impact is limited to certificate validation within the same component and does not affect system availability.

notes.text: The Go standard library function net/url.Parse insufficiently validated the host/authority component and accepted some invalid URLs by effectively treating garbage before an IP-literal as ignorable. The function should have rejected this as invalid.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: Incorrect parsing of IPv6 host literals in net/url
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat evaluates this vulnerability as having an Important severity because unauthenticated remote attackers can target exposed Go services over the network to trigger severe denial-of-service conditions or validation discrepancies without requiring elevated privileges. Across standard Red Hat environments—including OpenShift Container Platform and Red Hat Enterprise Linux container tools—many components rely on the core Go runtime to process user-supplied addresses and endpoints. Although improper handling of malformed host segments in web addresses can disrupt network-facing daemons, the vulnerability cannot be leveraged for arbitrary code execution or data leakage, keeping the risk bounded within the Important classification.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go standard library packages `crypto/x509` and `crypto/tls`. During the process of building a certificate chain, an attacker can provide a large number of intermediate certificates. This excessive input is not properly limited, leading to an uncontrolled amount of work being performed. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) condition, making the affected system or application unavailable to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: crypto/tls: golang: Go: Denial of Service vulnerability in certificate chain building
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go standard library's certificate chain building process. Systems utilizing Go applications that process untrusted TLS certificates or X.509 certificate chains are susceptible to resource exhaustion when presented with an excessive number of intermediate certificates, potentially leading to service unavailability. This flaw impacts applications directly using `crypto/x509` or `crypto/tls`.

cwe.name: Multiple Releases of Same Resource or Handle

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net` package of Go (golang), specifically when using the `LookupCNAME` function with the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a very long Canonical Name (CNAME) response. This can trigger a double-free of C memory, leading to a crash and a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net: golang: Go net package: Denial of Service via long CNAME response in LookupCNAME
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go `net` package, affecting applications configured to use the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could trigger a double-free memory error by providing a very long CNAME response, leading to a crash of the vulnerable application and impacting service availability.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata relevant to your system have been applied.

For details on how to apply this update, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

To mitigate this issue, applications can be configured to use the pure Go DNS resolver instead of the `cgo` DNS resolver. This can be achieved by setting the `GODEBUG` environment variable to `netdns=go`. For example, to run a Go application with this mitigation: `GODEBUG=netdns=go /path/to/your/go/application`. This change may require restarting affected applications or services to take effect. Users should verify that this change does not negatively impact DNS resolution for their specific application environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in zod. A remote attacker can trigger a denial of service (DoS) by submitting an excessively large array of invalid items to an application that validates input schemas without length constraints. Because the validation process accumulates error records for each failing element without a cap or early exit, the application consumes excessive memory and crashes due to an out-of-memory condition.

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated with an Important severity because remote attackers can induce complete service unavailability through process termination without requiring privileged access. Within Red Hat environments, the affected library is embedded into multiple management consoles and microservices that process structured user data. The operational impact depends on whether exposed network endpoints evaluate untrusted collections without preliminary restrictions on payload sizes or element counts.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri. This vulnerability arises because fast-uri does not correctly interpret backslash characters as authority delimiters in Uniform Resource Locators (URLs), unlike Node.js's native WHATWG URL parser. This discrepancy can cause applications that use fast-uri for security policy enforcement, such as allowlists or Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) filtering, to misidentify the intended host. Consequently, an attacker could bypass these security policies, potentially redirecting traffic to unintended internal or sensitive network destinations.

This could enable an attacker to redirect traffic to unintended internal or sensitive network destinations.

notes.text: A validation flaw has been discovered in the python cryptography package. This missing validation allows an attacker to provide a public key point P from a small-order subgroup. This can lead to security issues in various situations, such as the most commonly used signature verification (ECDSA) and shared key negotiation (ECDH). When the victim computes the shared secret as S = [victim_private_key]P via ECDH, this leaks information about victim_private_key mod (small_subgroup_order). For curves with cofactor > 1, this reveals the least significant bits of the private key. When these weak public keys are used in ECDSA , it's easy to forge signatures on the small subgroup. Only SECT curves are impacted by this.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw, while difficult to exploit, would lead to a loss of integrity in the encrypted communication channel. Given that the cryptography package is a library, it is likely to be used in situations that do not require user interaction.

Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fflate. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted ZIP archive. This archive, when processed, can lead to an infinite loop during decompression, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) condition. This occurs because a malformed central directory entry in the ZIP archive causes out-of-bounds reads, which keeps a processing loop permanently active.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fflate: fflate: Denial of Service via crafted ZIP archives
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This CVE describes a denial-of-service flaw in the fflate JavaScript compression library. Parsing a maliciously crafted ZIP archive via unzipSync()/unzip() triggers an infinite loop in the ZIP64 central-directory parser (z64e): a central directory entry declaring the ZIP64 size sentinel (0xFFFFFFFF) but omitting the required ZIP64 extra field causes out-of-bounds reads that keep the loop condition permanently true, consuming CPU indefinitely. Only fflate's ZIP-extraction APIs are affected; its gzip/deflate/zip-creation paths are not.

Red Hat products bundle fflate almost exclusively within web-frontend assets. Each affected component was assessed individually. Components that reach fflate only through compression-only consumers (posthog-js gzip telemetry, jsPDF zlib) never invoke the vulnerable unzipSync/z64e path and are marked not affected (vulnerable code not in the execute path). Components that bundle fflate in the vulnerable version range (through 0.8.2) where the ZIP-extraction path could not be positively excluded are marked affected. Where the vulnerable path is reachable only from client-side browser code processing same-origin assets, practical impact is limited to a self-inflicted denial of service within the user's own browser session rather than a service-level outage.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. Its custom parser for bracketed IPv6 literals does not fully validate the IPv6 grammar, allowing invalid trailing text in an authority to be silently discarded. This can lead to a malformed, attacker-controlled host being normalized into a different, valid IPv6 destination, such as a local or private IPv6 target. An application normalizing untrusted URLs before outbound requests, redirects, or proxy routing could be redirected, resulting in a server-side request forgery (SSRF) and address-policy bypass.

This could allow an attacker to bypass URL allowlists or network-based access controls, potentially enabling unauthorized access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or other network resources. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a software component used for parsing Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) in Node.js applications. This vulnerability arises from an issue in how fast-uri processes the scheme part of a URI, specifically when it contains special characters that are percent-encoded. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious URI, causing the parser to misinterpret the host, which can lead to serious security risks. These risks include unauthorized redirection to external websites, server-side request forgery (SSRF) where the application makes unintended requests to internal or external resources, and bypassing security policies.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: URI parsing flaw enables server-side request forgery and redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A host confusion vulnerability was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. The parser runs a legacy decoding pass over the scheme component and never re-escapes the result. As a consequence, an input whose scheme carries percent-encoded slashes parses as having no authority (undefined host), yet resolving or normalizing that same input emits a network-path reference with an attacker-chosen authority. Applications that normalize or resolve untrusted URLs before a redirect check, host allowlist, or outbound request decision can be steered to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF), open redirect, or address-policy bypass. Additionally, a normalized URI in a response header can carry injected carriage return line feed (CRLF) characters, enabling HTTP response splitting attacks such as cache poisoning or session hijacking. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.
notes.title: Statement

The vulnerability occurs because the urllib.parse.parse_qs function is used without limiting the maximum number of fields.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tornado's request body parsing mechanism. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an HTTP request with an excessively large number of form field key-value pairs. Parsing these fields synchronously blocks Tornado's single-threaded event loop, leading to a complete denial of service for all concurrent connections and incoming requests.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in node-forge. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to forge valid RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures for arbitrary messages. The flaw occurs because the software fails to properly validate the element count in nested DigestAlgorithm sequences during signature verification. By embedding specially crafted data, an attacker can bypass signature validation, leading to potential integrity compromise.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: node-forge: node-forge: Signature forgery vulnerability in RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 verification
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as having an Important impact because an attacker can remotely forge valid signatures to subvert cryptographic integrity checks without holding the private signing key. In Red Hat environments, node-forge is vendored into various management web consoles and Node.js-based services where signature verification is performed. Successful exploitation requires the verifier to process RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures using small public exponents (such as e=3), allowing Bleichenbacher-style forgery through malformed ASN.1 parsing. Systems utilizing standard exponents like 65537 or alternative signature mechanisms are not susceptible to this attack.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. A remote server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by initiating a Transport Layer Security (TLS) renegotiation and presenting a certificate with a mismatched hostname. Because the client application fails to properly handle the resulting verification error, an uncaught assertion is triggered, terminating the client process and disrupting active network requests.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Denial of Service via TLS renegotiation with mismatched certificate
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as an Important severity flaw for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote server can terminate a client Node.js process, halting all concurrent tasks and in-flight operations. In typical Red Hat deployments, containerized microservices and administrative consoles rely on undici or runtime fetch APIs to communicate with external web endpoints. Exploitation requires the client application to establish an outbound TLS 1.2 connection to a malicious or compromised endpoint that initiates session renegotiation with a non-matching certificate. Workloads communicating strictly with trusted endpoints or utilizing TLS 1.3 connections are inherently protected, as TLS 1.3 does not permit server-driven renegotiation.

notes.text: A flaw was found in proxy-addr. When an application defines trusted proxy subnets using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses with an improper prefix length, the subnet parser fails open and erroneously treats all incoming network addresses as trusted. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a forged X-Forwarded-For header to spoof their client IP address. This flaw allows attackers to bypass IP-based access controls, rate limiting, and audit logging.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: proxy-addr: proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because unauthenticated remote attackers can spoof client IP addresses and circumvent security controls, such as rate limits or network access lists, by sending custom forwarding headers. Exploitation is contingent on application configurations that define reverse proxy trust subnets using IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation with short IPv4 prefix lengths. Environments configuring trusted proxies via canonical IPv4 CIDR blocks, hostnames, or default loopback addresses are not vulnerable to this behavior.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

To mitigate this flaw through configuration:

1. Configure trusted proxy definitions using standard IPv4 notation (such as `10.0.0.0/8`) rather than IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation.
2. If IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation is required, set the subnet prefix length to at least 97 to cover the mapped boundary (for example, specify `::ffff:10.0.0.0/104` instead of `::ffff:10.0.0.0/8`).
3. Alternatively, sanitize or strip incoming `X-Forwarded-For` headers at edge load balancers or boundary reverse proxies before passing traffic to backend applications.

Warning: Modifying application configuration files requires restarting the Node.js application service, which will temporarily interrupt service availability and active connections.

cwe.name: Insecure Preserved Inherited Permissions

notes.text: A flaw was found in adm-zip. This vulnerability allows privilege escalation when untrusted archives are extracted with original file permissions enabled. The library fails to filter out special Unix execution flags, such as setuid or setgid, from extracted files. If an administrative process extracts a specially crafted archive, an attacker can place a binary that allows a local unprivileged user to execute code with administrative privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: adm-zip: adm-zip: Privilege escalation via unfiltered permission bits in extracted archives
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A local privilege escalation flaw rated IMPORTANT by Red Hat was found in the adm-zip JavaScript library, which is bundled by several Red Hat products for creating and extracting ZIP archives. When extracting a ZIP archive with the keepOriginalPermission option enabled, adm-zip applies the Unix permission bits stored in the archive entry to the extracted file without filtering out the setuid and setgid bits. An attacker who can supply a specially crafted archive to an application or process that extracts it with this option enabled, for example a build, CI, or installation step running with administrative privileges, can cause a binary with the setuid bit set to be written to disk. If a local unprivileged user subsequently executes that file, the attacker's code runs with administrative privileges, resulting in a full compromise of the confidentiality and integrity of the affected host. Red Hat rates this flaw with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.1 (AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N), consistent with the upstream severity. Fixes for affected Red Hat product streams, including OpenShift Container Platform and community Fedora and EPEL components, are being pursued through the responsible product teams. Red Hat Enterprise Linux is not affected because the vulnerable adm-zip code is not present in the shipped gjs packages, and in the JBoss Fuse 7 ELS stream the vulnerable code is not in an executable path.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: nltk: nltk: Arbitrary file write via path traversal in WekaClassifier
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate path traversal vulnerability was found in the Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) WekaClassifier module, which affects Red Hat AI offerings that ship the nltk Python package, including Red Hat Lightspeed and OpenShift AI (RHOAI) components. The WekaClassifier does not validate the model_filename and model path arguments, so an attacker who can control these arguments can bypass the nltk.pathsec directory containment and cause the Weka JVM to write arbitrary files (via the -d option) or probe for existing files (via the -l option) outside of the allowed data directories. Successful exploitation requires an application to pass attacker-controlled paths to the WekaClassifier interface in an environment where the Weka JVM is available, which limits practical exposure; the impact is primarily high integrity loss through unauthorized file writes, with limited confidentiality and availability impact. While the upstream CVE record rates this flaw as Important, Red Hat classifies it as Moderate because exploitation depends on an application exposing the WekaClassifier interface to untrusted path input in a configured Weka environment. The affected Red Hat products are considered vulnerable, and a fix is being pursued through the responsible product teams.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Write

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Google Brotli decoder. An out-of-bounds write in the block-type switch handling in c/dec/decode.c can be triggered by a crafted Brotli-compressed stream. When an application decompresses untrusted Brotli data, this can lead to memory disclosure, denial of service, or potentially arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: brotli: Out-of-Bounds Write in Google Brotli Decoder
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This issue is rated Important. Exploitation requires that the target decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data (for example HTTP content negotiated with Content-Encoding: br, or APIs such as Node.js zlib / fetch() that decode Brotli). The vulnerable path is reached with a malformed stream rather than typical well-formed encoder output. Red Hat Enterprise Linux compiler and runtime hardenings - including Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), Non-eXecutable (NX) memory, FORTIFY_SOURCE, and SELinux - increase the difficulty of turning this memory corruption into reliable code execution, though they do not eliminate crashes or all impact. Combined with the Attack Requirements noted by the CNA (CVSS v4 AT:P), Red Hat scores Attack Complexity as High and rates the flaw Important rather than Critical.

---

The Node.js packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux use either system version of brotli or bundled version. Some Node.js versions are marked "Not affected" because they utilize system brotli. For these versions, the Node.js package itself does not require updating. However, customers must still update the system brotli/libbrotli package to address the vulnerability for these Node.js installations.

Following is the overview of Node.js versions use system or bundled version.

- Node.js 22 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, provided via nodejs:22 module, uses system brotli.
- Node.js 24 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and 9, provided via nodejs:24 modules, use bundled brotli.
- Node.js 22 and 24 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, provided via nodejs22 and nodejs24 use system brotli.

---

The .NET packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux may either use system version of brotli or bundled version. Following is the overview of .NET versions use system or bundled version.

- .NET 8.0 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, provided via dotnet8.0 packages, use bundled brotli.
- .NET 9.0, 10.0, and 11.0 in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, provided via dotnet9.0, dotnet10.0, and dotnet11.0 packages, use system brotli.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted Microsoft Image Composer (MIC) file. When an application attempts to count or extract frames from the malicious image, an improper state reset triggers an infinite loop. This non-advancing loop consumes excessive CPU resources and can hang application worker processes indefinitely.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can induce an infinite loop, exhausting worker CPU resources and resulting in a denial of service for applications handling untrusted image data. Exploitation requires the optional olefile dependency to be present to register the Microsoft Image Composer format handler, and specifically targets workflows that query frame counts or process multi-frame images. Environments that do not inspect frame counts or do not have olefile installed are not vulnerable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. The PDF parser fails to limit recursion depth when reading nested PDF data structures such as arrays and dictionaries. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted, deeply nested PDF file to an application processing PDFs in append mode. This causes excessive recursion that crashes or terminates the worker process, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in PDF parser

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker could cause worker process termination and denial of service by submitting maliciously structured input files. However, exploitation is constrained to specific deployment workflows where an application utilizes Pillow to append image data onto preexisting, untrusted PDF documents. Systems and services that only process standard raster image formats or do not manipulate external PDF files in append mode are unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by submitting a zero-size image to an application that applies rank-based filters, such as median, minimum, or maximum filters. When attempting to expand the image borders, Pillow reads from unallocated image storage, resulting in an application crash.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as having an impact of Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash backend application processes handling image transformations without requiring elevated privileges. In Red Hat environments deploying services with Pillow, processing untrusted image inputs or crop coordinates using rank-derived filtering routines can lead to service interruption. However, the scope of impact is confined strictly to process termination resulting from an invalid memory dereference, with no evidence of memory corruption or confidentiality exposure.

Exposure is largely concentrated in containerized services and image-processing pipelines that handle untrusted animation uploads directly.

In typical Red Hat environments, such as containerized AI or automation workloads processing image data, processing oversized transformation geometries under strict process memory limits forces premature deallocation of internal structures, culminating in process termination. Applications that sanitize image bounds or avoid exposing custom affine transform endpoints remain largely unaffected by this crash condition.

cwe.name: NULL Pointer Dereference

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a specially crafted image file to an application that processes images with the library. This issue occurs because the Image.merge() function fails to properly validate the first input band, allowing mismatched image storage formats to trigger a null pointer dereference. Consequently, processing the malformed image causes the native application process to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via null pointer dereference in Image.merge()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash service worker processes handling user uploads without requiring privileges or prior interaction. In Red Hat environments such as Ansible Automation Platform, Satellite, and OpenShift AI, Pillow is embedded across containerized services and platform tooling that handle image ingest and transformation. Because parsing an invalid image file triggers an immediate segmentation fault within the native extension, the issue causes service disruption, although it does not compromise data confidentiality or allow arbitrary code execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When rendering text using FreeType with an active stroke width, a failure during glyph loading can cause the library to free an uninitialized or stale memory pointer. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying a malformed font to an application that renders stroked text. Successful exploitation can lead to memory corruption or an application crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via invalid pointer free during font rendering
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as having an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker could cause memory corruption or terminate the application process without requiring privileges, leading to a denial of service. Across Red Hat product environments, Pillow operates as an underlying imaging component in automated services and containerized workloads. The vulnerability is only triggered if an application accepts untrusted font files from users and renders text using non-zero stroke widths, leaving services that utilize standard system fonts unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When converting multi-frame images into a multi-page PDF document, the library repeatedly scans previously assigned object identifiers, resulting in quadratic processing time. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying a crafted image with a large frame count, causing excessive CPU consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Denial of Service via crafted multi-frame image conversion

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can cause severe CPU exhaustion and service disruption by submitting minimal crafted inputs without needing system privileges. The elevated risk arises because even tiny files with declared high sequence numbers can tie up backend worker processes for prolonged periods in applications that convert user-provided graphics into multipage documents. Deployments remain unaffected if they only perform standard single-image rendering, validation, or do not expose multi-frame document export capabilities to untrusted users.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an unauthenticated remote attacker can cause severe service disruption and denial of service without requiring elevated privileges. Red Hat products shipping Pillow—including components within Red Hat OpenShift AI, Ansible Automation Platform, and Satellite—are exposed only when configured to append images to untrusted, user-supplied PDF documents. Standard deployments that do not append to external PDF files or that generate new documents from trusted sources are unaffected.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Read

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. When saving or re-encoding a Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) image containing inconsistent color map metadata, the encoder reads beyond an allocated memory buffer. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a specially crafted image, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or information disclosure of heap memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: Pillow: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds read in TIFF encoder
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can supply crafted image files over network endpoints to cause process termination or heap memory disclosure without requiring privileges. The impact primarily concerns applications and containerized services that ingest untrusted image data and subsequently re-encode or save it using the libtiff-backed encoder while retaining metadata. Environments and workflows that only read, validate, or display images without writing them back out to TIFF format are not affected.

cwe.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource

notes.text: A flaw was found in Pillow. This flaw can lead to information disclosure when handling compressed Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) images. During incomplete decoding of image data, uninitialized buffer memory is not cleared before being converted into pixel rows. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted TIFF image to an application that decodes and returns or re-encodes the image, allowing them to view stale contents from heap memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pillow: pillow: Information disclosure via uninitialized buffer in TIFF decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this vulnerability as Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit default image parsing workflows to extract sensitive process memory without requiring privileges or triggering application crashes. In Red Hat environments such as Red Hat OpenShift AI and Ansible Automation Platform, backend services that ingest user-provided images and return rendered thumbnails, previews, or re-encoded files inadvertently disclose previously freed heap data from concurrent or prior operations. The vulnerability requires processing compressed TIFF files where the decoder handles truncated image streams, meaning services that reject this format or never expose generated image outputs are not impacted.

notes.text: A flaw was found in filelock. When utilizing the ReadWriteLock mechanism, the component reopens SQLite database and auxiliary files by file path rather than retaining secure file descriptors. A local attacker with file renaming permissions in a shared directory can swap these filenames during operation, causing the application to delete or overwrite unintended files. This issue can result in unauthorized data modification, data loss, or a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: filelock: filelock: Arbitrary file overwrite via insecure database file reopening
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate severity rather than Important because successful exploitation requires local account access and non-standard directory permissions where untrusted users can manipulate filenames within an unsticky parent directory. Under standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux installations, default kernel settings such as fs.protected_regular and fs.protected_hardlinks restrict link manipulation in common shared locations like /tmp. In addition, exposure is limited to workloads configured to utilize the SQLite-backed ReadWriteLock mechanism rather than standard single-process locking.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows an attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution by supplying an untrusted submodule path. Because the library fails to properly validate destination paths before cloning repository data, an attacker can plant a malicious executable script into sensitive directories, such as the Git hooks folder. Subsequent Git operations then trigger the planted script, executing commands in the context of the running application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: GitPython: GitPython: arbitrary code execution via improper submodule path validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because successful exploitation permits arbitrary code execution within the context of the underlying service or container. Although execution of arbitrary commands represents a critical consequence, the rating reflects the high complexity and prerequisites required, specifically that an application must accept user-controlled submodule paths and operate where default Git hook templates are absent. In Red Hat environments, such as Ansible Automation Platform, OpenShift AI, and Red Hat Satellite, impact is limited to workloads configured to process repository structures from untrusted or unauthenticated sources.

Red Hat build of MicroShift release 4.19.53 is now available with updates
to packages and images that include a security update.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact
of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score,
which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability
from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Red Hat build of MicroShift is Red Hat's light-weight Kubernetes
orchestration solution designed for edge device deployments and is built
from the edge capabilities of Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform.
MicroShift is an application that is deployed on top of Red Hat Enterprise
Linux devices at the edge, providing an efficient way to operate
single-node clusters in these low-resource environments.

This advisory contains the RPM packages for Red Hat build of MicroShift
4.19.53. Read the following advisory for the container images for this
release:

https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:89655

Security Fix(es):

* encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive
recursion in Unmarshal (CVE-2026-33818)
* mime: golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME
header (CVE-2026-42504)
* html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via
pathological input (CVE-2026-56858)
* net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic
complexity in path resolution (CVE-2026-56860)
* crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite
KeyUpdate messages (CVE-2026-56862)
* crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted
intermediate certificates (CVE-2026-111943)

All Red Hat build of MicroShift 4.19 users are advised to use these updated
packages and images when they are available in the RPM repository.

cwe.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Excessive Platform Resource Consumption within a Loop

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) package. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words. This could lead to excessive CPU consumption, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: mime: golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME header
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is rated as an Important severity flaw. A remote attacker could trigger a Denial of Service by sending a crafted MIME header with numerous invalid encoded-words to an application utilizing the affected Golang MIME package. This could lead to excessive CPU consumption on the system processing the malformed header, impacting service availability.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_build_of_microshift/4.19/html/red_hat_build_of_microshift_release_notes/index

To mitigate this issue, restrict network access to services that process MIME headers from untrusted sources. Implement input validation and sanitization for all incoming data, especially MIME headers, to prevent maliciously crafted content from being processed by applications utilizing the vulnerable Golang MIME package.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Excessive Platform Resource Consumption within a Loop

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text:
Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes v2.13 general availability release images, which provide security fixes, bug fixes, and updated container images.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.
A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE links in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes provides the
capabilities to address common challenges that administrators and site
reliability engineers face as they work across a range of public and
private cloud environments. Clusters and applications are all visible and
managed from a single console—with security policy built in.

This advisory contains the container images for Red Hat Advanced Cluster
Management for Kubernetes, which add new features and enhancements, bug
fixes, and updated container images. See the following
Release Notes documentation, which will be updated shortly for this
release, for additional details about this release:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.13/html-single/release_notes/index#acm-release-notes

notes.text: On instances using Auth Proxy header authentication ([auth.proxy]) with identity caching enabled (sync_ttl > 0), two distinct user identities could produce the same cache key. An authenticated low-privileged user able to influence their own forwarded identity attributes could be served a higher-privileged user's cached session and act as that user for the duration of the cache TTL. Default configurations are not affected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: Grafana: Session takeover via Auth Proxy cache key collision
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important impact because successful exploitation allows an authenticated user to hijack sessions of administrative or privileged accounts, leading to complete compromise of the application. The flaw requires non-default settings where reverse proxy header-based authentication is enabled alongside active identity caching. In standard Red Hat product deployments, header-based proxy authentication is not enabled by default, which substantially limits the attack surface across standard installations.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Grafana. When extracting plugin archives, Grafana did not safely resolve symbolic links. A remote attacker could craft a malicious plugin archive with symbolic links to escape the plugin installation directory. This allows the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute malicious code with the privileges of the Grafana server process, leading to remote code execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: grafana: PLUGIN ARCHIVE EXTRACTION ESCAPES THE PLUGIN DIRECTORY, ALLOWING CODE EXECUTION
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Grafana's plugin extraction process is vulnerable to symbolic link traversal, enabling an attacker to write arbitrary files and achieve remote code execution with the privileges of the Grafana server. This critical flaw allows malicious code execution even before plugin signature verification, posing a significant risk in Red Hat deployments where Grafana is used.

remediations.details: While no configuration fully mitigates this issue, exposure can be reduced by limiting plugin installations to vetted and pinned sets of plugins from trusted sources. Additionally, disable the `plugin_admin_enabled` setting in the Grafana configuration if not required, to prevent non-administrator users from installing plugins. This can be done by setting `plugin_admin_enabled = false` in the `[plugins]` section of the `grafana.ini` configuration file. A restart of the Grafana service may be required for changes to take effect, which could temporarily impact service availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in grpc-gateway up to v2.28.0. A remote attacker could exploit an incorrect access control vulnerability by sending a specially crafted POST request that includes the X-HTTP-Method-Override header. The application processes this header without restricting allowed methods, allowing the request method to be rewritten to an arbitrary attacker-supplied value before routing. This bypasses method-based access controls enforced by upstream proxies or Web Application Firewalls (WAFs), potentially leading to unauthorized actions or information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway: github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2: grpc-gateway: Access control bypass via X-HTTP-Method-Override header
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate impact for Red Hat products because exploitation requires a deployment where upstream reverse proxies or perimeter filters enforce access control solely based on HTTP methods without stripping method-override headers. In typical Red Hat deployments, backend gRPC services enforce their own authentication and authorization controls, limiting an attacker's ability to execute unauthorized actions simply by tunneling rewritten request verbs.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. The component failed to properly enforce source-address restrictions for several authentication methods, including password and keyboard-interactive callbacks. In applications that misuse the ServerConfig.PublicKeyCallback callback to make security relevant authorization decisions, an attacker with a valid key could bypass network-based access controls to gain additional privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Authentication bypass due to unenforced source-address restrictions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability severity is Important due to the requirement that an attacker already have a valid private key. A flaw in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh allows remote attackers to bypass source-address restrictions for certain authentication methods. This would allow an attacker to use a valid key for gaining additional privileges outside of the bounds of the network-based access controls.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/xml` package of Go. The `DecodeElement` function failed to correctly track recursion depth, which could lead to stack exhaustion. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML input, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important denial of service flaw affects applications utilizing the Go `encoding/xml` package. This vulnerability arises from an issue in XML decoding where a recursion depth counter fails to reset, potentially leading to stack exhaustion when processing malicious XML input.
