notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost/compress package. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted compression dictionary with an excessively large repeat value, triggering an integer overflow. When the dictionary is subsequently processed, this overflow leads to out-of-bounds memory access, crashing the application and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via integer overflow in dictionary processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as having an impact of Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker could trigger a denial of service by causing a process crash without requiring elevated permissions. In Red Hat environments where this Go library is embedded, exploitation requires that an application accepts untrusted dictionary structures for S2 compression and subsequently attempts encoding. Although the resulting memory access fault terminates the vulnerable process, the flaw is confined to process crashes and does not compromise data confidentiality or integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in kin-openapi, a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. An unauthenticated client can exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted query with a large index in a deepObject query parameter. This forces the application to allocate multi-gigabyte memory, leading to an Out-of-Memory (OOM) error or a restart loop, effectively causing a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/getkin/kin-openapi: kin-openapi: Denial of Service via uncontrolled resource consumption in deepObject query parameter decoding
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Important because a small request can exhaust memory and terminate an exposed service. Exploitation requires an application to decode attacker-controlled query parameters using kin-openapi’s deepObject handling with an array-containing schema. Schema limits such as maxItems do not prevent the allocation, and HTTP handler panic recovery does not protect against process termination from memory exhaustion.

notes.text: A flaw was found in RabbitMQ amqp091-go. The tlsConfigFromURI helper creates tls.Config values for amqps:// URIs without setting MinVersion. When the client is built with a Go toolchain whose default still permits TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1, a network attacker who can influence TLS negotiation may force an obsolete protocol version and weaken protection of AMQP messages and credentials. The issue is fixed in amqp091-go 1.13.0 by requiring TLS 1.2 as the minimum.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Missing Explicit TLS Minimum Version Configuration In URI Parser
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Red Hat product streams that ship amqp091-go before 1.13.0 are Affected because tlsConfigFromURI does not set an explicit TLS MinVersion when parsing AMQPS URIs. Exploitation requires a man-in-the-middle position on the path to the AMQP broker; Go 1.18 or later client defaults further raise complexity by preferring TLS 1.2 when MinVersion is unset. Streams that already ship amqp091-go 1.13.0 or later contain the explicit fix and are Not affected. The issue is not Critical because it is not remotely exploitable without those high-complexity prerequisites, and it does not provide unauthenticated remote code execution.

notes.text: RabbitMQ amqp091-go versions before 1.13.0 mishandle an oversized AMQP longstr field. A malicious or compromised broker can desynchronize message parsing, causing subsequent bytes to be interpreted as AMQP data and disrupting connection integrity or availability. Fixed in version 1.13.0.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go: RabbitMQ amqp091-go: Protocol Desynchronization and Frame Injection via Integer Overflow in readLongstr
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw affects Red Hat products using the vulnerable RabbitMQ amqp091-go client. Exploitation requires a malicious or compromised AMQP broker and may disrupt client connections or cause unintended protocol processing. Red Hat rates this issue Important.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust process memory by sending millions of fragmented HTTP/2 DATA frames. Each fragmented frame is stored as a separate message, consuming disproportionate heap memory. This can lead to a runtime panic or out-of-memory termination, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via HTTP/2 DATA Frame Fragmentation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust memory and crash affected applications without exceeding connection flow-control windows. Within Red Hat OpenShift and containerized platforms, gRPC-Go is embedded in various internal control plane agents, monitoring exporters, and management components. Although services handling untrusted remote gRPC traffic remain susceptible to denial of service, exposure in standard cluster deployments is constrained because these interfaces typically operate across isolated internal networks or behind mutual TLS boundaries.

notes.text: A flaw was found in js-yaml, a JavaScript YAML parser. An attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted YAML document that causes the parser to perform excessive processing when handling merge keys with empty sources. This can lead to prolonged CPU consumption, effectively causing a denial of service (DoS) for applications that process untrusted YAML input.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: js-yaml: js-yaml: Denial of Service vulnerability in YAML parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in js-yaml, affecting applications that process untrusted YAML input. The flaw allows an attacker to craft a small YAML document that, when parsed, can lead to prolonged CPU consumption due to inefficient merge key processing, potentially exhausting system resources. This is particularly relevant where applications handle external YAML data and have merge processing enabled by default.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.

notes.text:
A flaw was found in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver for version < 1.17.10 and < 2.9.1. 
Improper handling of data query elements in the GridFS component can lead to a file identifier being misinterpreted as a query. An authenticated user can exploit this to delete all GridFS file chunks, making stored file content unreadable, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the MongoDB Go Driver. The GridFS component does not properly sanitize caller-supplied file identifiers before using them in database queries. A structured document passed as a file ID (for example, a BSON document containing query operators) is interpreted as a query condition rather than a literal match value. An authenticated attacker who can influence the file identifier passed to GridFS operations such as Delete, DownloadToStream, or OpenDownloadStream in an affected application can exploit this to delete all chunks in a GridFS bucket, resulting in permanent data loss and denial of service.
The practical impact depends on whether the product's code passes externally-controlled values as GridFS file identifiers.

- Validate file identifiers before passing them to GridFS operations. Ensure that file IDs supplied by users or external systems are scalar values (e.g., primitive.ObjectID or string) and reject any structured BSON documents or maps. This prevents query operator injection.
- Restrict who can supply GridFS file identifiers. Do not allow unauthenticated or low-privilege users to directly control the file ID parameter in GridFS API calls (Delete, OpenDownloadStream, DownloadToStream, etc.).

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve cached responses, including sensitive session credentials like Set-Cookie values, belonging to other users. This occurs because the component fails to properly validate security-zeroed cache entries when processing client `max-stale` directives. By requesting the same URL with a large `max-stale` value, an attacker can obtain another user's session credentials from shared-cache entries that were intended to be secure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: http-cache-semantics: http-cache-semantics: Information Disclosure via max-stale directive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can bypass shared-cache security controls over the network and expose sensitive session credentials belonging to other users. Red Hat products vendoring this library in client-only command-line tools or local development utilities are at reduced risk, as triggering the defect depends on an intermediary or shared cache mechanism processing client cache-control directives. Environments hosting multi-tenant web applications or reverse proxies that evaluate HTTP cache headers via this component face direct exposure to cross-session credential disclosure.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. The lookupProperty own-property check returns Function.prototype.constructor before the prototype-method deny list is applied. When an attacker can render a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault enabled and an accessible function in the template context, arbitrary JavaScript can execute with the application process privileges.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via Own Property Check Bypass
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires rendering a controlled template with allowProtoMethodsByDefault set to true (off by default) and an accessible function in the template context, allowing bypass of the constructor deny list via Function.prototype. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because those non-default runtime conditions raise attack complexity (AC:H); default Handlebars configurations that keep allowProtoMethodsByDefault disabled are not exploitable for this issue.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. Incomplete validation of pre-parsed AST objects passed to compile() or precompile() allows unchecked AST fields to be emitted into generated JavaScript. An attacker who can supply an object instead of a template string can inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: handlebars: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion in compile (Program.blockParams)
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires an application to pass a non-string object (for example, a JSON-deserialized value) to Handlebars.compile() or Handlebars.precompile(). Applications that only pass template strings are not affected. When that unsafe calling pattern is present, injected JavaScript can run with the privileges of the Node.js process. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because successful exploitation depends on that non-default API usage condition (AC:H), not on typical string-template pipelines alone.

notes.text:
Red Hat multicluster engine for Kubernetes v2.8 general availability release images, which provide security fixes, bug fixes, and updated container images.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.
A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE links in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
The multicluster engine for Kubernetes provides the foundational components
that are necessary for the centralized management of multiple
Kubernetes-based clusters across data centers, public clouds, and private
clouds.

You can use the engine to create new Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
clusters or to bring existing Kubernetes-based clusters under management by
importing them. After the clusters are managed, you can use the APIs that
are provided by the engine to distribute configuration based on placement
policy.

cwe.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `os.Root` functionality of Go on Unix systems. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass intended directory restrictions by crafting a path that ends with a symbolic link and a trailing slash. When a file is opened in `os.Root` with such a path, the symbolic link is improperly followed, potentially leading to access to locations outside of the defined root directory. This could result in information disclosure or unauthorized file system access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in Go's os.Root implementation. On Unix systems, `os.Root.Open()` improperly follows symlinks to locations outside the root directory when the path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., root.Open("symlink/")). This is because `openat()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` does not prevent symlink resolution when the path has a trailing /. An attacker able to create symlinks within an os.Root directory could use this to read or write files outside the intended root. The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected. This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

The following symbols are affected:
* `OpenInRoot`: Opens a file or directory within an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Create`: Creates a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Open`: Opens a path relative to an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenFile`: Opens a file with specified flags and permissions inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenRoot`: Opens a sub-root directory from an `os.Root`.
* `Root.ReadFile`: Reads a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.WriteFile`: Writes a file inside an `os.Root`.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

cwe.name: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information

notes.text: A flaw was found in http-cache-semantics. This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve cached responses, including sensitive session credentials like Set-Cookie values, belonging to other users. This occurs because the component fails to properly validate security-zeroed cache entries when processing client `max-stale` directives. By requesting the same URL with a large `max-stale` value, an attacker can obtain another user's session credentials from shared-cache entries that were intended to be secure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: http-cache-semantics: http-cache-semantics: Information Disclosure via max-stale directive
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having Important severity for Red Hat products because remote, unauthenticated attackers can bypass shared-cache security controls over the network and expose sensitive session credentials belonging to other users. Red Hat products vendoring this library in client-only command-line tools or local development utilities are at reduced risk, as triggering the defect depends on an intermediary or shared cache mechanism processing client cache-control directives. Environments hosting multi-tenant web applications or reverse proxies that evaluate HTTP cache headers via this component face direct exposure to cross-session credential disclosure.

cwe.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code

notes.text: A flaw was found in Handlebars. Incomplete validation of pre-parsed AST objects passed to compile() or precompile() allows unchecked AST fields to be emitted into generated JavaScript. An attacker who can supply an object instead of a template string can inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript in the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has an Important impact. Exploitation requires an application to pass a non-string object (for example, a JSON-deserialized value) to Handlebars.compile() or Handlebars.precompile(). Applications that only pass template strings are not affected. When that unsafe calling pattern is present, injected JavaScript can run with the privileges of the Node.js process. The issue is not Critical for Red Hat scoring because successful exploitation depends on that non-default API usage condition (AC:H), not on typical string-template pipelines alone.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

cwe.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: Important: A flaw in the Go `crypto/tls` package allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service in applications using TLS 1.3. By sending multiple key update messages in a single record post-handshake, an attacker can trigger a connection deadlock, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption. This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net` package of Go (golang), specifically when using the `LookupCNAME` function with the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a very long Canonical Name (CNAME) response. This can trigger a double-free of C memory, leading to a crash and a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go `net` package, affecting applications configured to use the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could trigger a double-free memory error by providing a very long CNAME response, leading to a crash of the vulnerable application and impacting service availability.

To mitigate this issue, applications can be configured to use the pure Go DNS resolver instead of the `cgo` DNS resolver. This can be achieved by setting the `GODEBUG` environment variable to `netdns=go`. For example, to run a Go application with this mitigation: `GODEBUG=netdns=go /path/to/your/go/application`. This change may require restarting affected applications or services to take effect. Users should verify that this change does not negatively impact DNS resolution for their specific application environment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Denial of Service via crafted HTTP Range headers
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. Across Red Hat enterprise environments, Go is widely deployed in container runtimes, monitoring daemons, and OpenShift infrastructure components. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go. Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. This vulnerability allows improper certificate validation, bypassing policy constraints via using ExtKeyUsageAny in VerifyOptions.KeyUsages.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: Usage of ExtKeyUsageAny disables policy validation in crypto/x509
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is rated as an Important severity because the vulnerability was found in the certificate validation logic of the Verify function. When VerifyOptions.KeyUsages includes ExtKeyUsageAny, certificate chains containing policy graphs may bypass certificate policy validation. This flaw allows an attacker to trick the system into accepting an invalid certificate, potentially enabling spoofing attacks, the issue weakens trust decisions in affected cases and impacts system integrity. Confidentiality and availability are not affected.

Red Hat Openshift Container Platform openshift-golang-builder-container ships golang 1.23 and does not ship the affected code.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in the crypto/tls component. This vulnerability occurs during Transport Layer Security (TLS) session resumption when certificate authority (CA) settings are modified between the initial and resumed handshakes. An attacker could exploit this to bypass certificate validation, allowing a client or server to establish a connection that should have been rejected. This could lead to an authentication bypass under specific conditions.

notes.text: This is a moderate flaw because it only occurs under specific conditions, such as TLS session resumption with runtime changes to certificate authority settings. Exploitation is not straightforward and requires a controlled setup. The impact is limited to certificate validation within the same component and does not affect system availability.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A certificate validation flaw has been discovered in the golang crypto/x509 module. When verifying a certificate chain which contains a certificate containing multiple email address constraints which share common local portions but different domain portions, these constraints will not be properly applied, and only the last constraint will be considered.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: Incorrect enforcement of email constraints in crypto/x509
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because unauthenticated network entities can bypass identity restrictions without requiring local system privileges. In Red Hat environments hosting Go-based network services or container infrastructure, certificate chain validation overlooks specific email name constraints when multiple rules share an identical local mailbox name across distinct domain names. As a result, a subordinate certificate authority could successfully issue unauthorized certificates that circumvent organizational security policies, leading to improper trust establishment.

cwe.name: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code

notes.text: A flaw was found in the cmd/compile package in the Go standard library. The compiler fails to correctly check for integer overflow or underflow in arithmetic operations involving loop induction variables. As a result, the compiler allows invalid memory indexing to occur at runtime, potentially leading to memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: cmd/compile: possible memory corruption after bound check elimination
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is only exploitable in applications that contain a loop structure that relies on an induction variable. An induction variable is a variable that gets modified, usually incremented or decremented, by a predictable amount on each iteration. Inside the loop, the induction variable must be directly used as the index to access or modify elements within an array or a slice. Additionally, an attacker must be able to cause an integer overflow or underflow in the induction variable to trigger this issue. Due to these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:

To mitigate this vulnerability, strictly sanitize and enforce bounds checking on any untrusted user input that influences loop counters, iteration limits, or memory indices. If there is no integer overflow or underflow, the out-of-bounds access cannot occur.

cwe.name: Expected Behavior Violation

notes.text: A flaw was found in the cmd/compile package in the Go standard library. A no-op interface conversion prevented the compiler from correctly identifying non-overlapping memory moves. As a result, the compiler allows unsafe memory move operations to occur at runtime, potentially causing data corruption, memory corruption or unexpected application behavior.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: cmd/compile: no-op interface conversion bypasses overlap checking
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is only exploitable in applications that contain a memory move or copy operation that is subject to a no-op (no-operation) interface conversion. Furthermore, the source and destination memory addresses involved in the move or copy must overlap and an attacker must be able to supply an input that triggers this specific operation. Due to these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go standard library packages `crypto/x509` and `crypto/tls`. During the process of building a certificate chain, an attacker can provide a large number of intermediate certificates. This excessive input is not properly limited, leading to an uncontrolled amount of work being performed. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) condition, making the affected system or application unavailable to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: crypto/tls: golang: Go: Denial of Service vulnerability in certificate chain building
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go standard library's certificate chain building process. Systems utilizing Go applications that process untrusted TLS certificates or X.509 certificate chains are susceptible to resource exhaustion when presented with an excessive number of intermediate certificates, potentially leading to service unavailability. This flaw impacts applications directly using `crypto/x509` or `crypto/tls`.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's `crypto/x509` package. A remote attacker could exploit this by presenting a specially crafted certificate chain containing a large number of policy mappings. This inefficient validation process consumes excessive resources, which can lead to a denial of service (DoS) for applications or systems performing certificate validation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: Go crypto/x509: Denial of Service via inefficient certificate chain validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw occurs during the validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains that contain a large number of policy mappings, leading to excessive resource consumption. Exploitation requires an attacker to present a specially crafted, yet trusted, certificate chain which would require the attacker has already compromised a trusted certificate root. Red Hat continuously monitors certificate authorities and curates the set which is trusted by default for Red Hat products.

cwe.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple key update messages in a single record after the handshake. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).

By sending multiple key update messages in a single record post-handshake, an attacker can trigger a connection deadlock, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption. This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package within Go (golang). When verifying a certificate chain, excluded DNS (Domain Name System) constraints are not correctly applied to wildcard DNS Subject Alternative Names (SANs) if the case of the SAN differs from the constraint. This oversight could allow an attacker to bypass certificate validation, potentially leading to the acceptance of a malicious certificate that should have been rejected. This issue specifically impacts the validation of trusted certificate chains.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important flaw in the Go `crypto/x509` package that could allow an attacker to bypass certificate validation. The vulnerability arises from an incorrect application of excluded DNS constraints to wildcard DNS Subject Alternative Names (SANs) when their case differs from the constraint. This could lead to Red Hat products accepting malicious certificates from otherwise trusted chains, compromising the trust model.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net` package of Go (golang), specifically when using the `LookupCNAME` function with the `cgo` DNS resolver. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a very long Canonical Name (CNAME) response. This can trigger a double-free of C memory, leading to a crash and a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net: golang: Go net package: Denial of Service via long CNAME response in LookupCNAME

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go `net` package, affecting applications configured to use the `cgo` DNS resolver. To mitigate this issue, applications can be configured to use the pure Go DNS resolver instead of the `cgo` DNS resolver. cwe.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP CONNECT request with a request body is rejected by a server, the client transport can desynchronize the connection before returning it to the shared idle pool. In shared reverse proxy environments, a remote attacker can exploit this issue to cause cross-user response poisoning, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to other users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of moderate impact was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped by a broad range of Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset components), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, OpenShift Container Platform and other Go-based components across Red Hat's portfolio. When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request that carries a non-empty request body, the body is written to the connection without framing after the request headers. If the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx keep-alive response, Transport returns the desynchronized connection to the shared idle pool, and the trailing body bytes can be interpreted by the server as a subsequent pipelined request. A remote attacker able to send requests through a reverse proxy (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forwards CONNECT requests via a shared Transport could exploit this to poison the responses received by other users of the pooled connection, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to them. Red Hat rates this flaw MODERATE (CVSS 6.5, limited confidentiality and integrity impact with no availability impact), which is lower than the CISA score of 7.5 (IMPORTANT) based on a confidentiality-only vector; Red Hat's assessment reflects that the exposure requires a shared reverse-proxy deployment that forwards CONNECT requests with bodies and yields low confidentiality and integrity impact. For most affected Red Hat products the fix is deferred because the flaw is rated MODERATE severity with a CVSS score below 7.0, so the residual risk of cross-user response poisoning in such proxy deployments remains until a fix is delivered; for a subset of affected products fixes are being pursued by their maintaining teams, and some affected streams are out of active support.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending HTTP/2 requests that declare an excessive number of trailer header fields. Because the server bypasses configured header limits when allocating memory for these declarations, an attacker can exhaust system memory resources and cause the application to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: net/http: Denial of Service via HTTP/2 trailer header memory exhaustion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A memory exhaustion flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP/2 client sends a "Trailer" header declaring a large number of trailer fields, the server allocates memory for each declared field when populating the Request.Trailer map, bypassing the Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending specially crafted HTTP/2 requests to exhaust server memory and cause a denial of service.

This issue only affects applications that operate an HTTP/2 server and process client-supplied trailer headers; HTTP/1 servers are not affected because they do not multiplex requests over a single connection and calculate header limits differently.

This flaw was fixed in Go 1.26.9 and 1.27.2 (net/http), and in golang.org/x/net/http2 v0.60.0 for code using the x/net module.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

There is no configuration-based mitigation for applications that must accept client-supplied trailer headers over HTTP/2. Possible mitigations are:
- Disable HTTP/2 in the affected server (e.g. do not configure http2 via TLSNextProto / do not serve over h2), forcing HTTP/1.1 where the issue does not apply.
- Terminate HTTP/2 at a reverse proxy or load balancer that limits request/header sizes and does not forward excessive trailer declarations to the backend.
- Restrict network access to the HTTP/2 endpoint so that only trusted clients can connect.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When operating as a reverse proxy, the HTTP/2 implementation does not properly validate framing-related headers in responses received from upstream servers before forwarding them to downstream HTTP/1 clients. A malicious upstream server can exploit this flaw by sending malformed response headers, resulting in HTTP response smuggling, where message boundaries between the proxy and client become desynchronized. This issue may allow attackers to bypass security controls, poison web caches, or intercept sensitive data from other user sessions.

notes.text: Red Hat has determined that this vulnerability affects products that use the Go `net/http` HTTP/2 implementation as a reverse proxy between an upstream server and an HTTP/1 client. Exploitation requires a malicious or compromised upstream server to send malformed framing-related response headers. Successful exploitation may allow HTTP response smuggling, which can bypass security controls or affect the integrity and confidentiality of proxied traffic. Red Hat is addressing affected products through the applicable security updates.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's HTTP/2 server implementation. A remote attacker can bypass connection-level flow control limits—mechanisms that regulate incoming network data—potentially causing excessive memory consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS). This issue occurs because the server improperly refunds flow control credits twice for the same data: once when a client resets a stream, and again when the application reads the buffered data. Consequently, a malicious client can exceed configured connection buffer limits.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass via double refund in HTTP/2 server
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because, while remote unauthenticated clients can bypass configured connection receive buffer thresholds on affected HTTP/2 servers, overall resource exhaustion remains bounded. Exploitation is constrained by stream-level flow controls and limits on concurrent streams, which prevents an attacker from causing unbounded memory consumption or a complete denial of service. Go-based network services handling untrusted HTTP/2 traffic may experience elevated memory usage under sustained reset attacks, but typical deployments remain operational without catastrophic service disruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

cwe.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP server sends a successful response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request without taking raw control of the connection, it improperly continues to process incoming data as standard HTTP requests instead of establishing a tunnel. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior to conduct HTTP request smuggling through intermediate proxy servers, potentially bypassing security controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: net/http: HTTP request smuggling via improper handling of HTTP/1 CONNECT responses
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate-impact flaw was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped in the golang and go-toolset components of Red Hat Enterprise Linux and used by many Go-based Red Hat products and components (including Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and bundled components such as osbuild-composer and rhc). When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the connection, the server improperly continues to read and serve HTTP requests from a connection that should be treated as an opaque tunnel. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server through an intermediate proxy that treats the connection as tunneled can exploit this desynchronization to conduct HTTP request smuggling, potentially bypassing proxy-enforced security controls and accessing requests or responses intended for other users. Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate severity (CVSS 3.1 base score 6.5, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N), reflecting the limited confidentiality and integrity impact. Because the impact is Moderate with a CVSS score below 7.0, fixes for the affected Red Hat products are currently deferred rather than scheduled for an immediate update, and the Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 2.0.z streams are out of support scope. The residual risk of deferral is limited to HTTP request smuggling against servers that accept HTTP/1 CONNECT requests and are deployed behind an intermediate proxy.

A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a crafted multipart form request that bypasses configured memory limits when the remaining boundary limit is small. This issue allows the application to read an arbitrarily long line into memory, leading to excessive resource consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS).

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate severity for Red Hat products because, while an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger excessive memory consumption leading to a denial of service, exploitation cannot lead to code execution or information disclosure. The issue specifically threatens Go-based services and daemons that accept and process incoming multipart HTTP form payloads. Applications built with Go that do not expose web interfaces or parse multipart request streams are unaffected by this flaw.

When a user works inside a malicious Go project that defines a bogus golang.org/fips140 module and connects to an untrusted Go module proxy (GOMODPROXY), the proxy can serve an arbitrary replacement module that still passes local verification. Successful exploitation can result in arbitrary code execution as the user running the go command.

Go versions before 1.24 do not include the bundled golang.org/fips140 module handling and are not affected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the html/template package in Go. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to conduct cross-site scripting (XSS, an attack that executes malicious scripts in a user's browser) through improper output escaping. When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the parser fails to properly reset its context tracking state. Consequently, subsequent regular expression literals are not accurately recognized and escaped, potentially allowing untrusted content to bypass template sanitization.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: golang: cross-site scripting via consecutive expressions in JavaScript template literals
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A MODERATE severity cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in Go's html/template package, which is shipped and used across multiple Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and other components that build against the Go toolchain. When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the parser fails to properly reset its context tracking state upon entering a new expression. As a result, subsequent regular expression literals are not accurately recognized and escaped, allowing a remote attacker to supply untrusted content through a template that bypasses html/template sanitization and executes malicious script in a victim's browser. Successful exploitation requires a victim user to visit a rendered page of a Go web application that interpolates attacker-controlled input into JavaScript template literals. Red Hat has rated this flaw MODERATE with a CVSS 3.1 score of 6.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N), consistent with the upstream assessment; the impact is limited to low confidentiality and integrity loss within the client browser context, with no availability impact. Because the CVSS score is below 7.0, the fix is deferred for the affected Red Hat product streams and update trackers are not being filed for this MODERATE severity flaw at this time. The residual risk is limited to Go-based web applications that render attacker-controlled content through html/template into JavaScript contexts; the flaw does not affect applications that do not use html/template with JavaScript template literals.

cwe.name: Race Condition within a Thread

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the HTTP/2 server. Due to missing synchronization, the server concurrently modifies its HPACK (HTTP/2 header compression) encoder when encoding response headers while processing incoming table size configuration updates. A malicious client can exploit this race condition by repeatedly sending requests while altering the header table size, ultimately causing the server process to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via concurrent HPACK encoder modification
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw is rated with a Moderate severity for Red Hat products because, although remotely triggerable without authentication, successful exploitation relies on winning a race condition and causes only a denial of service without compromising system confidentiality or integrity. Within Red Hat environments, exposure is limited to network services and server applications built with the Go runtime that actively handle HTTP/2 connections. Applications communicating strictly over HTTP/1.1 or where client connections do not modify header compression parameters are not vulnerable.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Disable HTTP/2 server processing in affected Go applications by setting the environment variable GODEBUG=http2server=0, or restrict network exposure to trusted clients.

For applications managed by systemd, configure the environment variable by creating a service override:

systemctl edit <service-name>

Add the following lines under the [Service] section:

[Service]
Environment="GODEBUG=http2server=0"

Apply the changes and restart the daemon:

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart <service-name>

To limit network exposure using firewalld, restrict access to trusted networks:

firewall-cmd --zone=trusted --add-source=<trusted-ip-range> --permanent
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveats:
Disabling HTTP/2 forces incoming client traffic to HTTP/1.1 and will break protocols that require HTTP/2, such as gRPC.

Warning: Reloading systemd configurations and restarting the service or firewall will briefly interrupt active network sessions and cause temporary service unavailability.

vulnerabilities.title: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via concurrent HPACK encoder modification

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Use of Uninitialized Variable

notes.text: A vulnerability was found in Golang FIPS OpenSSL. This flaw allows a malicious user to randomly cause an uninitialized buffer length variable with a zeroed buffer to be returned in FIPS mode. It may also be possible to force a false positive match between non-equal hashes when comparing a trusted computed hmac sum to an untrusted input sum if an attacker can send a zeroed buffer in place of a pre-computed sum.  It is also possible to force a derived key to be all zeros instead of an unpredictable value.  This may have follow-on implications for the Go TLS stack.

notes.text: golang-fips: Golang FIPS zeroed buffer
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is specific to the Go language and only affects the test code in cri-o and conmon, not the production code. Since both projects use Go exclusively for testing purposes, this issue does not impact their production environment. Therefore, cri-o and conmon are not affected by this vulnerability.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in the crypto/tls component. This vulnerability occurs during Transport Layer Security (TLS) session resumption when certificate authority (CA) settings are modified between the initial and resumed handshakes. An attacker could exploit this to bypass certificate validation, allowing a client or server to establish a connection that should have been rejected. This could lead to an authentication bypass under specific conditions.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is a moderate flaw because it only occurs under specific conditions, such as TLS session resumption with runtime changes to certificate authority settings. Exploitation is not straightforward and requires a controlled setup. The impact is limited to certificate validation within the same component and does not affect system availability.

cwe.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go standard library packages `crypto/x509` and `crypto/tls`. During the process of building a certificate chain, an attacker can provide a large number of intermediate certificates. This excessive input is not properly limited, leading to an uncontrolled amount of work being performed. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) condition, making the affected system or application unavailable to legitimate users.

Systems utilizing Go applications that process untrusted TLS certificates or X.509 certificate chains are susceptible to resource exhaustion when presented with an excessive number of intermediate certificates, potentially leading to service unavailability. This flaw impacts applications directly using `crypto/x509` or `crypto/tls`.

cwe.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

cwe.name: Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple key update messages in a single record after the handshake. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).

By sending multiple key update messages in a single record post-handshake, an attacker can trigger a connection deadlock, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption. This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.
